overview: Media servers decode, mix into one composite stream per participant and re-encode.

estimation.assumption: Illustrative room: 10 publishers each sending 1 Mbps.
estimation.calculation: SFU ingress ≈ 10 Mbps; forwarding everyone to everyone costs up to 10 × 9 = 90 Mbps egress.
estimation.result: Layer selection and active-speaker limits reduce egress; MCU trades bandwidth for encode CPU.
estimation.implication: Size media servers by packet/egress or codec compute separately from signaling connections.

entityDetails.purpose: Meeting control-plane state, permissions and media-region assignment.
accessPatterns: Create/join a meeting; authorize participants; end a session.
constraints: Short-lived join tokens bind identity, meeting and media region. Media packets do not pass through this SQL database.

apiDetails.rationale: Recording permissions and retention are explicit; allocate a nearby media region.

apiDetails.purpose: Authorize a participant and return media-session credentials.
apiDetails.rationale: Signaling exchanges SDP/ICE over WebSockets; RTP media goes to SFU/MCU or TURN, independently of the API.
Use ICE with STUN/TURN; WebSocket signaling does not carry the video media stream.

flows.title: Join and negotiate an MCU session

steps.title: Participants → Signaling LB → Meeting Service → Meetings
steps.explanation: Authorize meeting membership and choose a region with enough codec capacity.

steps.title: Participants → STUN/TURN
steps.explanation: Use TURN relay when NAT blocks the media connection.

steps.title: Participants → Media LB → Regional MCU
steps.explanation: MCU decodes inputs, mixes a layout and encodes an adaptive composite. Clients receive fewer streams at higher server CPU cost.

steps.title: Regional MCU → Recording bots → Recordings
steps.explanation: Persist authorized composite recordings under the meeting retention policy.

failureCases.scenario: A participant changes network or the media node fails
failureCases.handling: Use ICE restart, reconnect signaling and reassign a healthy media node/region with a new token. Expect a short media interruption; preserve meeting permissions and roster.

alternatives: Use an SFU when server bandwidth is cheaper than encoding CPU and clients decode multiple streams. Use an MCU when light clients or composed output justify mixing and re-encoding latency.
